core_meaning.primary_meaning: Muiz corresponds to the Arabic form مُعِزّ and is glossed in this record as “One who honours, giver of honour.” The record associates the form with root ع ز ز (ʿ-z-z). The lexical gloss describes the word-form; Qur’anic occurrence, religious recommendation, popularity, and a name-bearer’s character are separate claims and are not established by this gloss alone.
core_meaning.literal_meaning: One who honours, giver of honour
core_meaning.meaning_explanation: Muiz corresponds to the Arabic form مُعِزّ (Arabic root ع ز ز (ʿ-z-z); مُعِزّ (Muʿizz)). Its core sense is muiz; one who honours, giver of honour. Muiz is Arabic مُعِزّ (Muʿizz) 'one who honours, giver of honour', from the root ع ز ز (ʿ-z-z). The source gloss 'Reviver, Reformer' is unsupported and has been replaced with the lexical sense. Same name as muizz.

persian.name: معز
persian.long_meaning: Muiz (معز) نامی برگرفته از زبان عربی است و معنای اصلی آن معز، عزت‌بخش است. این نام در جوامع مسلمان به کار می‌رود و کاربرد آن بسته به بافت زبانی متفاوت است.

hindi.name: मुइज़्ज़

faq.q: What is the root of Muiz?

faq.a: In Urdu it is written معز and carries the sense “معز، عزت دینے والا”.

faq.a: Documented usage records Muiz as a boy's name; actual use can vary by community.
